title: Transmission temperature signal indicates extreme heat
plainEnglishMeaning: The PCM received a transmission-temperature signal representing extreme heat. Actual overheating and an electrical or sensor fault must be separated by testing.
enableCriteria: The reproduced Roadmaster chart states 148 °C or higher for five seconds.
failureCriteria: Transmission-fluid-temperature input remains at the extreme-hot end of its range.
pcmFallbackAction: Illuminate the malfunction indicator and substitute a 90 °C transmission-temperature value.
driverSymptoms: Shift timing or torque-converter-clutch operation may be affected by the substituted temperature value.

likelyCauses.cause: Transmission temperature sensor out of calibration

falsePositiveConditions: A grounded signal wire can look like extreme fluid temperature.
confirmatoryTests: Compare the scan value with the transmission's actual temperature.
Inspect the signal circuit for a short to ground.
Check sensor resistance against the applicable temperature-to-resistance table.
safetyLevel: Stop and investigate if actual overheating is confirmed
